Peppard Road.road: Main B-road (B481), two-way with white centre line, fairly wide; side-road junctions with give-way lines; long stretches lined by woodland, high walls and hedges with grass verges.
Peppard Road.note: A long tree-lined main road: many stretches are just woodland or hedge, with interwar semis (some mock-Tudor gables, rendered upper floors), a red-brick Victorian lodge, modern red-brick detached houses and a few bungalows set well back behind hedges and fences.

Mayfield Drive.road: Two-way residential street, no centre line, moderate width, gentle curves; wide grass verges on one side with lamp posts; on-street parking, many paved front drives.
Mayfield Drive.note: Uniform 1950s semis with hipped brown tiled roofs: red brick ground floor and cream/white rendered first floor, bay windows, low red brick walls and paved drives, grass verges along the pavement.

Lowfield Road.road: Long distributor road, two-way, fairly wide, dashed white centre line and give-way junctions with turn arrows at the Caversham Park Road end; long stretches with a grass verge and woodland/hedge on one side.
Lowfield Road.note: 1960s-70s Caversham Park estate housing: red-brown brick link-detached and terraced houses with white-clad or rendered first floors and integral garages on open-plan front gardens, plus a few newer detached houses; much of the road edge is woodland, hedge or fence.

Kingsway.road: Narrow-to-medium estate road, two-way, no centre line; dead-end sign and give-way markings at the junction; paved front drives and some double yellow lines near the entry, otherwise on-street parking.
Kingsway.note: 1970s Caversham Park estate: orange-brown and buff brick semis and short terraces with white weatherboard/clad first-floor panels, shallow brown concrete-tiled roofs, integral garages and open-plan block-paved drives.

Galsworthy Drive.road: Two-way estate loop road, no centre line, moderate width; give-way markings at junctions; on-street parking and many block-paved/concrete front drives; tall hedges along some side boundaries.
Galsworthy Drive.note: 1960s-70s Caversham Park estate: orange-brown and buff brick terraces, semis and link-detached houses with white-clad or rendered first-floor panels, shallow concrete-tile roofs, integral garages and open drives; one remodelled white-rendered house.

Chiltern Road.road: Two-way residential road, fairly wide, no centre line; wide grass verges with young street trees between pavement and road; 'KEEP CLEAR' marking at a side entrance; double yellow lines near the Henley Road end.
Chiltern Road.note: 1930s semis with hipped tiled roofs and bays: red brick ground floors with white or cream rendered upper floors, some fully rendered, a few with mock-Tudor gables; low brick walls and hedges, wide grass verges with trees, and a newer red-brick house at the north end.

Grosvenor Road.road: Only the two ends were visible, at junctions with main roads (B481 Peppard Road and A4155): those are wide two-way roads with centre lines and turn arrows; Grosvenor Road itself has no Street View imagery (likely private/unadopted).
Grosvenor Road.note: No Street View along Grosvenor Road itself; the end views show tall hedges, fences and big trees, with red-brick Victorian/Edwardian houses and an interwar mock-Tudor gabled semi near the A4155 end.

Woods Road.road: Quiet two-way residential road, no centre line, moderate width, pavements both sides with kerbs; on-drive parking.
Woods Road.note: Leafy road of 1930s-60s detached houses, semis and chalet bungalows: red brick, some white-rendered, a mock-Tudor gable or two, dark/brown tiled roofs with dormers, behind tall hedges or low white-painted walls and gravel drives.

Harlech Avenue.road: Narrow two-way estate cul-de-sac road, no centre line, curving; small grass verges, brick-paved drives, parking on drives.
Harlech Avenue.note: 1970s Caversham Park estate: orange/red-brown brick two-storey link-semis, short terraces and a few detached houses with shallow brown/grey concrete-tiled roofs, white garage doors and porch canopies, open-plan lawns and block-paved drives with some panel fences.

All Hallows Road.road: Two-way residential road, no centre line, moderate width; wide grass verges with large mature street trees, give-way lines at junctions, cars on drives.
All Hallows Road.note: Leafy interwar road: red-brick and white-rendered 1930s semis and detached houses with hipped dark/brown tile roofs, some chalet bungalows with dormers and the odd mock-Tudor house, behind hedges, low walls and picket fences, with wide verges and big trees.

Milestone Way.road: Not a normal street in the views: one end is an unmade gravel lane/footpath between hedges and fences; other views snapped onto Harlech Avenue (estate cul-de-sac) and Northbrook Road (two-way with dashed centre line, edged by dense woodland/hedge).
Milestone Way.note: Seems to be a footpath/lane threading through the Caversham Park estate rather than a built-up street; what houses show are 1970s orange-brown brick estate semis and terraces with brown concrete-tile roofs behind panel fences and hedges.

Hawthorne Road.road: Quiet two-way residential road, no centre line, moderate width; a grassy triangle/green at a junction with give-way lines, pavements, cars on drives.
Hawthorne Road.note: Low-density road of detached chalet bungalows and houses, many white-rendered with steep dark/brown tiled roofs and dormers, others red brick, set behind clipped hedges and low brick walls with lawns and a grassy green at the junction.

Queensway.road: Two-way estate road, no centre line, curving; double yellow lines at the corners, block-paved and gravel drives, some grass verges and mature trees, panel fences along side gardens.
Queensway.note: 1960s-70s Caversham Park estate: light orange/buff brick terraces and link-semis with white weatherboard-clad first floors, shallow grey/brown concrete-tile roofs, flat-roofed garages and porches, open-plan front gardens and block-paved drives, with panel fences at the side gardens.

The Horse Close.road: Small two-way cul-de-sac, no centre line, ending in a circular turning head with a grass island and lamp post; narrow grass verges, cars on drives.
The Horse Close.note: 1950s-60s cul-de-sac of red-brick semis and detached houses plus a few chalet bungalows with dormers, brown/dark tiled roofs, some white-painted ground floors, behind low picket/trellis fences, small brick walls and open lawns.

Holyrood Close.road: Two-way estate close, no centre line, moderate width; grass verges, block-paved and concrete drives, one end opens onto a large grassed playing field.
Holyrood Close.note: 1970s Caversham Park estate close: red, orange and buff brick link-detached houses and semis with white-clad panels under first-floor windows, shallow gabled brown/grey concrete-tile roofs, integral and flat-roofed garages, open-plan lawns and block-paved drives with a few panel fences.

Orchard Grove.road: Narrow two-way cul-de-sac road, no centre line, curving, with block-paved/tarmac drives, small grass verges and a few mature oaks.
Orchard Grove.note: 1980s-90s developer estate: small red and buff/yellow brick detached, semi and short-terrace houses with steep dark-brown concrete-tile roofs, gabled porch canopies, white bay windows and attached garages, on open-plan lawns.

Greystoke Road.note: No Street View imagery: all four views came up black with 'No Street View imagery available here' (both points, retried); likely a private/unadopted road off Peppard Road.

Osterley Drive.road: Narrow estate cul-de-sac, no centre line, small parking bays at the end; panel fences and conifer hedges along side gardens, open lawns and paved drives at the fronts.
Osterley Drive.note: 1970s Caversham Park estate: light orange/buff brick link-semis and short terraces with white weatherboard-clad first floors, shallow brown/grey concrete-tile roofs, integral garages and porch canopies, open-plan lawns; several views see only tall panel fences and conifers.

Valentine Crescent.road: Two-way residential crescent, no centre line, moderate width; narrow grass verge strips by the kerb, cars on paved/gravel front drives.
Valentine Crescent.note: 1930s semis with hipped brown/dark tiled roofs and bay windows topped by tile-hung red bay panels: a mix of red brick, white or cream render and pebbledash, some red-brick ground floors with rendered upper floors, behind low brick walls and picket fences.

Netley Close.road: Narrow estate cul-de-sac, no centre line, small turning head; small lawns, block-paved drives, a few panel fences and hedges.
Netley Close.note: 1970s Caversham Park estate close: light orange/buff brick link-semis and short terraces with white weatherboard-clad first floors, shallow brown concrete-tile roofs with tiled porch/garage canopies, integral garages with coloured doors, open-plan lawns.

Copse Avenue.road: Narrow two-way residential road, no centre line, partly without pavement on one side; overgrown hedges and grass edges, a school 'no stopping' sign near the end.
Copse Avenue.note: Low-density mix of detached red-brick houses and chalet bungalows (1950s-80s), some with dark-stained or tile-hung upper gables and steep brown/dark tiled roofs, set behind tall hedges, conifers and low fences.
